en.title: Chawanmushi — Savoury Steamed Egg Custard
en.description: A delicate Japanese steamed egg custard suspended in dashi with small pieces of chicken, shrimp, mushroom and fish cake. The signature texture is almost silken: a balanced egg-to-dashi ratio, straining and very gentle steam prevent holes and curdling.
en.animeContext: Inspired by the careful home-cooking focus of Today's Menu for the Emiya Family. No exact chawanmushi episode is claimed without direct scene evidence.

steps.prep_fillings: Cut chicken and shiitake into small pieces. Quickly blanch or sear the chicken until the exterior is no longer raw, and briefly blanch the shrimp if they are thick; the gentle custard steam should finish, not rescue, large cold raw fillings.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Season lukewarm dashi with usukuchi, mirin and a small pinch of salt. Let it cool to lukewarm or room temperature; hot stock can begin setting the egg before the mixture is strained.
steps.mix_eggs: Break the eggs and stir gently with chopsticks or a whisk without beating air into them. Measure roughly 100 ml egg for two large eggs and use about 250 ml dashi for the classic soft set.
steps.strain_fill: Combine egg and seasoned dashi slowly, then pass through a fine sieve. Divide chicken, shrimp, shiitake and kamaboko between two heatproof cups and pour in the custard to about three-quarters full; pop or skim surface bubbles.
steps.steam: Cover the cups. Steam over high heat for about 2 minutes to heat them, then reduce to very gentle steam for 10–12 minutes. The water should not violently boil around the cups or the custard will turn porous.
steps.check_finish: The surface should be smooth and set while the centre gives a delicate wobble. Insert a thin skewer: clear broth should appear around it, not raw egg. Garnish with mitsuba and serve warm.

it.title: Chawanmushi — Crema salata all’uovo al vapore
it.description: Una delicata crema salata giapponese all’uovo e dashi, con piccoli pezzi di pollo, gamberi, funghi e kamaboko. La consistenza deve essere quasi setosa: rapporto corretto tra uovo e brodo, filtraggio e vapore molto dolce evitano buchi e coagulazione ruvida.
it.animeContext: Ispirato all’attenzione per la cucina domestica di Today's Menu for the Emiya Family. Non attribuiamo il chawanmushi a un episodio preciso senza una verifica diretta della scena.

steps.prep_fillings: Taglia pollo e shiitake in piccoli pezzi. Sbollenta o scotta rapidamente il pollo finché l’esterno non è più crudo e, se i gamberi sono grandi, sbollentali brevemente: il vapore delicato della crema deve completare la cottura, non recuperare grossi ripieni freddi e crudi.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Condisci il dashi tiepido con usukuchi, mirin e poco sale. Lascialo arrivare a temperatura tiepida o ambiente: un brodo troppo caldo inizierebbe a coagulare l’uovo prima del filtraggio.
steps.mix_eggs: Rompi le uova e mescolale delicatamente con bacchette o frusta senza incorporare aria. Due uova grandi danno circa 100 ml: usa circa 250 ml di dashi per una consistenza morbida classica.
steps.strain_fill: Unisci lentamente uova e dashi condito, poi filtra con colino fine. Distribuisci pollo, gamberi, shiitake e kamaboko in due tazze resistenti al calore e versa la crema fino a circa tre quarti; elimina le bolle in superficie.
steps.steam: Copri le tazze. Cuoci a vapore forte circa 2 minuti per scaldarle, poi riduci a vapore dolcissimo per 10–12 minuti. L’acqua non deve bollire violentemente attorno alle tazze, altrimenti la crema diventa porosa.
steps.check_finish: La superficie deve essere liscia e rappresa, mentre il centro oscilla delicatamente. Inserendo uno stecchino deve affiorare brodo limpido, non uovo crudo. Completa con mitsuba e servi caldo.

es.title: Chawanmushi — Flan salado al vapor
es.description: Flan salado japonés de huevo y dashi con pequeños trozos de pollo, gambas, setas y kamaboko. La proporción, el colado y el vapor suave crean textura sedosa.
es.animeContext: Inspirado en la cocina doméstica de Today's Menu for the Emiya Family; no se afirma un episodio exacto.

steps.prep_fillings: Corta pollo y shiitake pequeños. Marca o blanquea el pollo y, si son grandes, las gambas; el vapor suave debe terminar la cocción.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Sazona dashi tibio con usukuchi, mirin y sal; no debe estar caliente.
steps.mix_eggs: Mezcla huevos suavemente sin aire. Para unos 100 ml de huevo usa aproximadamente 250 ml de dashi.
steps.strain_fill: Combina y cuela. Reparte rellenos, vierte la crema y elimina burbujas.
steps.steam: Tapa, cocina 2 minutos con vapor fuerte y luego 10–12 minutos con vapor muy suave.
steps.check_finish: Debe cuajar liso y temblar en el centro; un pincho debe liberar caldo claro, no huevo crudo.

fr.title: Chawanmushi — Flan salé vapeur
fr.description: Flan salé japonais à l’œuf et dashi, avec poulet, crevette, champignon et kamaboko. Ratio, filtrage et vapeur douce donnent la texture soyeuse.
fr.animeContext: Inspiré de la cuisine familiale de Today's Menu for the Emiya Family; aucun épisode précis n’est revendiqué.

steps.prep_fillings: Coupez poulet et shiitake petit. Saisissez ou blanchissez le poulet et, si grosses, les crevettes; la vapeur douce termine la cuisson.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Assaisonnez le dashi tiède avec usukuchi, mirin et sel; il ne doit pas être chaud.
steps.mix_eggs: Mélangez doucement les œufs sans air. Environ 100 ml d’œuf pour 250 ml de dashi.
steps.strain_fill: Mélangez, filtrez, répartissez les garnitures et versez la crème en éliminant les bulles.
steps.steam: Couvrez, vapeur forte 2 minutes puis très douce 10–12 minutes.
steps.check_finish: La crème doit être lisse, prise et légèrement tremblante; un pic doit faire sortir du bouillon clair.

de.title: Chawanmushi — Herzhafter Eierflan
de.description: Zarter japanischer Eier-Dashi-Flan mit Huhn, Garnele, Pilz und Kamaboko. Verhältnis, Sieben und sehr sanfter Dampf erzeugen die seidige Textur.
de.animeContext: Von der sorgfältigen Hausküche in Today's Menu for the Emiya Family inspiriert; keine konkrete Episode wird behauptet.

steps.prep_fillings: Huhn und Shiitake klein schneiden. Huhn und bei großen Garnelen auch diese kurz blanchieren oder anbraten; sanfter Dampf soll nur fertig garen.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Lauwarmes Dashi mit Usukuchi, Mirin und Salz würzen; nicht heiß verwenden.
steps.mix_eggs: Eier sanft ohne Luft verrühren. Etwa 100 ml Ei mit rund 250 ml Dashi verwenden.
steps.strain_fill: Mischen, fein passieren, Einlagen verteilen, Eierbrühe angießen und Blasen entfernen.
steps.steam: Abdecken, 2 Minuten kräftiger und dann 10–12 Minuten sehr sanfter Dampf.
steps.check_finish: Glatt gestockt mit sanftem Wackeln in der Mitte; am Stäbchen soll klare Brühe, kein rohes Ei erscheinen.

pt.title: Chawanmushi — Creme salgado de ovo no vapor
pt.description: Creme salgado japonês de ovo e dashi com frango, camarão, cogumelo e kamaboko. Proporção, coagem e vapor suave dão textura sedosa.
pt.animeContext: Inspirado na cozinha caseira cuidadosa de Today's Menu for the Emiya Family; não afirmamos episódio específico.

steps.prep_fillings: Corte frango e shiitake pequenos. Sele ou branqueie o frango e, se grandes, os camarões; o vapor suave deve apenas terminar a cocção.
steps.mix_seasoned_dashi: Tempere dashi morno com usukuchi, mirin e sal; não use quente.
steps.mix_eggs: Misture os ovos suavemente sem incorporar ar. Para cerca de 100 ml de ovo use aproximadamente 250 ml de dashi.
steps.strain_fill: Misture, coe, distribua recheios, despeje o creme e elimine bolhas.
steps.steam: Tampe, cozinhe 2 minutos com vapor forte e depois 10–12 minutos com vapor bem suave.
steps.check_finish: Deve ficar liso, firme e tremer levemente no centro; um palito deve liberar caldo claro, não ovo cru.
